newsitem.title: USA: Republicans join Clinton for chemical weapons pact.
newsitem.headline: Republicans join Clinton for chemical weapons pact.

text.p: Several Republican luminaries joined Democratic President Bill Clinton on Friday in urging U.S. Senate approval by an April 29 deadline of a treaty banning the manufacture, stockpiling or use of chemical weapons.

James Baker, secretary of state under President George Bush, retired Gen. Colin Powell and former Kansas Sen. Nancy Kassebaum-Baker joined Clinton at a campaign-style rally to press for passage of the Chemical Weapons Convention, which faces serious opposition in the Senate.

Baker pointed out that the treaty had been negotiated under former Republican Presidents Ronald Reagan and George Bush, and said it was "outrageous" to suggest either of them would act against the best interests of the United States.

"If we fail to ratify the Chemical Weapons Convention, we will be sending a clear signal of retreat from international leadership both to our allies and our enemies alike. This is a message we should never, never send," Baker said.

The treaty was signed by the United States and 129 other countries in Paris on Jan. 12, 1993. Although at last count 161 countries had signed and about 70 ratified the treaty, it has languished in the U.S. Senate since 1993. If the Senate fails to approve it by April 29, the United States will lose the right to be regarded as a charter signatory, which backers say would severely restrict the U.S. role in enforcing it.

Clinton thanked those who spoke at the White House lawn rally for helping him send "a clear, unambiguous, united message" on the issue. He added: "This is in the beginning a question of whether we will continue to make America's leadership strong and sure as we chart our course in a new time. We have to do that and we can only do that if we rise to the challenge of ratifying the Chemical Weapons Convention."
